boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Homewood destinations for group work, quiet study, recreation, meals, meetings, and outdoor breaks, selected from current Johns Hopkins sources.

cards.title: Build a Club Day Around the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Meeting, rehearsal, performance, dining, and downtime space at Homewood
cards.notes: Use the open seating between commitments, then check the center’s listings for reservable meeting, rehearsal, gaming, or performance spaces.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose student hub where nonacademic campus life can share one address.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins describes the Bloomberg Student Center as a 150,000-square-foot community hub on the Homewood campus.
cards.access_notes: Consult the center’s official visit information and posted building policies before arriving; room access may vary by space or event.

cards.title: Match the Room to the Assignment
cards.subtitle: Quiet reading, group rooms, teaching rooms, and café seating
cards.notes: Choose the quiet reading room for solo work or arrange a group room when conversation is part of the assignment; verify current access first.
cards.short_summary: A library complex designed to support both concentrated reading and collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Sheridan Libraries states that Brody connects to the Eisenhower Library and contains a large quiet reading room, 16 group study rooms, teaching and seminar rooms, and a café.
cards.access_notes: Library access and hours can change; consult the official location page and observe any J-Card restrictions.

cards.title: Use the Annex for a Long Study Block
cards.subtitle: A high-capacity library study location with practical equipment
cards.notes: Settle here when you need varied seating, printing, or vending nearby; confirm the current library schedule before planning an overnight session.
cards.short_summary: A large-capacity alternative when a study session needs seating and basic support close at hand.
cards.evidence_claim: The current Homewood study-spaces page lists the MSE Library Annex with 300 seats, varied seating, vending machines, and printer/copier machines.
cards.source_title: Homewood Campus Study Spaces - Sheridan Libraries
cards.access_notes: The cited 24/7 listing applied to the university’s Spring 2026 study-space update; verify current hours and J-Card access before relying on it.

cards.title: Read Beneath the Stained Glass
cards.subtitle: Gilman Hall’s historic reading room, known as “The Hut”
cards.notes: Bring reading that benefits from a quiet setting, and pause to examine the 19 printer-seal windows without disrupting other people’s work.
cards.short_summary: A historic reading room where Gilman Hall’s architectural detail frames focused study.
cards.evidence_claim: Sheridan Libraries identifies the Hutzler Reading Room in Gilman Hall and documents its 19 stained-glass windows bearing early European printers’ seals.
cards.source_title: Albert D. Hutzler Reading Room - Sheridan Libraries
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s official location page for current hours and access conditions; maintain reading-room quiet.

cards.title: Make Levering a Between-Class Base
cards.subtitle: A long-serving Homewood gathering place linked to the Glass Pavilion
cards.notes: Use Levering for a meal break, a conversation, or a fireplace study session, and check room rules before joining an event or group activity.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus gathering building that still supports meals, study, and organized activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins reports that Levering Hall has served as a Homewood student hangout and gathering place and is connected to the Glass Pavilion.
cards.source_title: The secret history of Johns Hopkins' original 'student center'
cards.access_notes: Building and event access can vary; follow posted university rules and any room-specific restrictions.

cards.title: Take the Work Outside at The Beach
cards.subtitle: The lawn near Homewood’s main entrance
cards.notes: Bring a portable task or meet classmates on the lawn during suitable weather; keep paths clear and leave the shared outdoor space as you found it.
cards.short_summary: A named campus lawn suited to informal conversation and fair-weather pauses.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins Admissions identifies The Beach as a lawn near the campus’s main entrance where students gather on warm, sunny days.
cards.source_title: Our Network of Campuses - Johns Hopkins University Admissions
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus lawn; use is weather-dependent and subject to campus events and posted restrictions.

cards.title: Bring a Small Group to CDI
cards.subtitle: A Homewood Apartments space with presentation tools
cards.notes: Use the wall whiteboard or portable projector for a small collaborative session, and contact the center before assuming the room is available.
cards.short_summary: A compact student-support setting that can also accommodate collaborative academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: The university’s Spring 2026 study-space listing placed the Center for Diversity and Inclusion at 3003 N. Charles Street, Suite 100, with 16 seats, a whiteboard, projector, and screen.
cards.source_title: Homewood Campus Study Spaces - Sheridan Libraries
cards.access_notes: The cited availability was temporary for Spring 2026 Reading and Exam Days; confirm current access directly with the center.

cards.title: Turn a Dining Room Into Group-Work Space
cards.subtitle: A large Charles Commons dining location used for exam-period study
cards.notes: Use the seating for collaborative review when the university designates it as study space, and do not assume that food service matches room access.
cards.short_summary: A dining venue that the university can repurpose as a sizable study setting during exams.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spring 2026 Homewood study-space update listed Nolan’s on 33rd with 200 seats and exam-period access extending beyond food-service hours.
cards.source_title: Homewood Campus Study Spaces - Sheridan Libraries
cards.access_notes: The cited extended access applied April 28–May 12, 2026; verify current dining-room access and food-service hours separately.

cards.title: Look Beyond the Main Library at Scott-Bates
cards.subtitle: A residence complex with designated exam-period study rooms
cards.notes: If you are not a resident, use only the entrance and rooms currently opened to all students; verify access before walking over with a group.
cards.short_summary: A residential destination that periodically opens specific rooms for broader student study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spring 2026 study-space page listed Scott-Bates Commons’ multipurpose room and Winter Library, identifying the Winter Library as open to all students via the 33rd Street entrance.
cards.source_title: Homewood Campus Study Spaces - Sheridan Libraries
cards.access_notes: The cited arrangement applied during Spring 2026 exams; residential access rules vary, so confirm eligibility and use the designated entrance.

cards.entity_name: Ralph S. O’Connor Center for Recreation and Well-Being
cards.title: Reset Between Classes at O’Connor
cards.subtitle: Recreation spaces ranging from courts to a climbing wall and outdoor seating
cards.notes: Pick an activity that fits your experience and membership access, or use the shaded picnic area for a daytime study break with classmates.
cards.short_summary: A recreation complex offering both active facilities and an outdoor place to regroup.
cards.evidence_claim: JHU Student Affairs describes O’Connor as an 80,000-square-foot Homewood facility and lists courts, fitness areas, climbing facilities, and a shaded outdoor picnic area with tables.
cards.source_title: Facilities - O’Connor Center for Recreation and Well-Being
cards.access_notes: Indoor facilities require applicable Recreation Center access; activities may require registration, training, a waiver, or reservations.
